title: Chicago school board president candidates Jessica Biggs, Hilario Dominguez, Victor Henderson have final forum before Election Day - ABC7 Chicago
text:
Chicago school board president candidates Jessica Biggs, Hilario Dominguez, Victor Henderson have final forum before Election Day - ABC7 Chicago 
 24/7 Live Chicago & Suburban Cook Co. North Suburbs West Suburbs South Suburbs NW Indiana Elections 
 Chicago school board president candidates meet for final forum before Election Day 
 Voters to choose CPS board president in first fully elected board election 
 Chicago school board president candidates Jessica Biggs, Hilario Dominguez and Victor Henderson attended a final forum Saturday before Election Day. By Lissette Nuñez Saturday, October 31, 2026 11:03PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google CHICAGO (WLS) -- Chicago voters are days away from choosing the president of the city's first fully elected school board as part of the upcoming midterm election.
 The three candidates for Chicago Board of Education president, Jessica Biggs, Victor Henderson and Hilario Dominguez, met at Rainbow PUSH Coalition for a Saturday morning forum ahead of Election Day.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Candidates were asked about a range of issues facing the district, including declining enrollment, financial stability, school consolidation, and student proficiency in math and reading.
 "The first thing that we need to do is fully fund our classrooms. We can't get better at reading without a reading specialist. Can't get better at math without a math specialist," Dominguez said.
 "Our financial challenges are real and they are current and I want to make sure that those challenges are resolved in way that is inclusive of our community's voices," Biggs said.

 "CPS is 10 billion in debt. Just this past year, they had a 735-750 million in debt. They are budgeting off money from Springfield that may not come, money from City hall that may not come. So either we want to have honest conversations and recognize that we have to make some tough choices," Henderson said.
 Biggs is a current school board member, a former special education teacher and a former principal at Burke Elementary on Chicago's South Side. Henderson is an attorney, the former president of the Chicago Bar Association and the outside ethics officer for the Chicago Housing Authority. Dominguez is a CPS graduate, a former special education teacher and the former deputy political director for the Chicago Teachers Union.
 With three days until Election Day, the candidates offered their final appeals to voters.
 "I am very proud to be the only person on this stage who has a voting record of independence. There it not a single special interest group that is happy every vote that I've taken, but I have centered students in every vote I have taken as a part of this board," Biggs said.
 "I'm independent. I have leadership skills. CPS needs that type of leadership right now. And so I'm the right person for the right time," Henderson said.
 "I ask voters to vote like they are protecting and fighting for our students especially our most vulnerable students especially our black and brown students," Dominguez said.
 Chicago voters will decide who will lead the city's first fully elected school board when they cast their ballots in the upcoming election.
